title: **Iran Accelerates Repairs on Hormozgan Bridges Destroyed by US Airstrikes, Key Routes to Reopen by Late September**
text:
"**Iran Accelerates Repairs on Hormozgan Bridges Destroyed by US Airstrikes, Key Routes to Reopen by Late September**"

"**BANDAR ABBAS, Iran** – Iranian road authorities have announced significant progress in rebuilding at least six strategic bridges in the southern province of Hormozgan that were destroyed during US airstrikes in mid-July, with officials confirming that major routes will be reopened to traffic within days."

"The attacks, which occurred on the night of July 16-17, marked the sixth consecutive night of American military strikes against Iranian territory. The US Central Command (CENTCOM) said the operations targeted military infrastructure, including coastal surveillance sites, air defense systems, and military logistics routes. However, the strikes hit multiple bridges in Bandar Khamir County, killing at least seven people and wounding several others, according to local authorities and state media, which later revised the death toll to eight."

"Among the damaged structures were the Geriveh (Gachin) Bridge, the Latidan (Kalmatli) Bridge, and the Kahurestan Bridge—a critical artery linking the major port city of Bandar Abbas to Shiraz and the interior Fars province. The Kahurestan crossing is particularly vital for commercial shipping and passenger transport, as Bandar Abbas sits on the strategic Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly one-fifth of the world's oil passes. Other bridges hit included two crossings on the Kahurestan-Lar road, a semi-finished bridge on the Bandar Khamir-Kashar axis, and a bridge near Maru village."

"In a statement to local media, Hormozgan's Road Administration provided a detailed update on the reconstruction effort. "The large Gachin bridge has been fully installed, and we are currently laying asphalt on its surface," an official said. "The Kahurestan bridge is also practically finished and will be reopened to traffic within this week.""

"Regarding the remaining damaged bridges, where traffic is currently being diverted through temporary side passages, authorities assured that all reconstruction work will be finalized by the end of Shahrivar, which corresponds to late September. The rapid repair timeline underscores the strategic importance of these road networks, as Iran moves to restore normalcy in the region following the extensive military campaign.
